$comment: Divergences between a convention snippet and a copy of it that this repository ships, which a
human has looked at and accepted. Checked by `npm run conventions:drift` and by
tests/convention-drift.test.mjs, which both fail on any drift that is NOT listed here.
AN ENTRY PINS BOTH SIDES. `snippetSha256` and `targetSha256` are sha256 over the section's
lines with line terminators and trailing blank lines normalised away — so a CRLF checkout
cannot move them, and editing EITHER text breaks the match and turns the check red. That is
the mechanism: an entry accepts two specific texts, never a convention's name. An exemption
keyed on the name alone would keep passing while the text underneath it rotted, which is the
failure this whole check exists to end.
`reason` is mandatory and must say WHY the two are allowed to differ, in a sentence a reader
who was not there can act on. An accepted divergence with no stated reason is indistinguishable
from one nobody ever looked at.
TO CHANGE ONE OF THESE TEXTS: make the edit, run `npm run conventions:drift`, read the new
fingerprints it prints, and update the entry — or delete the entry if you reconciled the two.
A stale entry is reported as an error, never ignored.

entries.reason: The two texts serve different readers and the SNIPPET is the stale side here, which is why this is recorded rather than propagated. templates/wiki/CLAUDE.md is the consigne scaffolded into a vault: it spells out each mode's full prompt template, and its binding paragraph was corrected to the workspaceBinding model (a bare OBSIDIAN_ROUTER_DEFAULT_VAULT line is a proposal the router reports and does not apply). The snippet is the condensed installable and still describes the binding model this router abandoned. Reconciling them is a content decision about what an installed convention should say, open as of 2026-09-11; until it is taken, both fingerprints are pinned so neither side can move unnoticed.
